claims.text: Machine-learning interatomic potentials will represent atomic configurations in ab initio liquids of multicomponent high-entropy alloys better than TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The improved configurational representation will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Better reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed method applies to both solid and liquid states at or near their high melting temperatures.
The applicable alloys contain 3–6 principal elements.
The applicable temperature range is 0.8–1.2 times the alloy melting temperature.
Atomic configurations and local-order parameters are the structural mediators of the proposed improvement.
Machine-learning potentials will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by 30% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The intervention will result in a free-energy difference of -0.1 eV/atom.
The accuracy of the machine-learning potentials depends on training-data quality.
The accuracy of the machine-learning potentials may depend on alloy-system complexity.
The hypothesis is falsified if the free-energy difference is not reduced by at least 20% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
